hints: Fix a letter and choose two columns.
A rectangle exists if two rows contain that letter in both chosen columns.
Remember previously seen column pairs; stop for that letter at the first repeated pair.
analogy: Each row stamps its pairs of matching-letter columns; a repeated stamp identifies the opposite corners of a rectangle.
example: In rows AAB and AAC, columns 1 and 2 contain A in both rows, so A has a valid rectangle.
algorithm: For each letter, initialize a bitset indexed by unordered column pairs. Scan rows, list the columns containing that letter, and enumerate their pairs. If a pair was already marked, answer YES; otherwise mark it. If all rows finish without a repeat, answer NO.
correctness: A marked pair means an earlier row had the letter in both columns. Seeing the same pair in another row gives four equal corners, and every valid rectangle produces exactly such a repeated pair.
complexity: For grid side n and k letters, O(k*n^2+n^2) time: before the first repeat each letter can mark at most n(n-1)/2 pairs. O(n^2) space for the grid and pair bitset.
